lines.text: Calder's wedding band cost two dollars.
As a boy, Alexander Calder made jewelry for his sister's dolls.
In 1929, he met Louisa James on an ocean liner.
lines.say: In nineteen twenty nine, he met Louisa James on an ocean liner.

lines.text: His first gift to her was a brass cuff spelling Medusa.
In 1930, he made her a gold spiral ring.
lines.say: In nineteen thirty, he made her a gold spiral ring.

lines.text: He thought it would do as a wedding ring.
Louisa called it her engagement ring instead.
So they bought a plain wedding band in Waltham for two dollars.
They married in 1931, and he gave her jewelry for birthdays.
lines.say: They married in nineteen thirty one, and he gave her jewelry for birthdays.

lines.text: The Metropolitan Museum showed his jewelry from 2008 to 2009.
lines.say: The Metropolitan Museum showed his jewelry from two thousand eight to two thousand nine.

post.caption: Calder's wedding band cost two dollars. As a boy, Alexander Calder made jewelry for his sister's dolls. In 1929, he met Louisa James on an ocean liner, and his first gift to her was a brass cuff spelling Medusa. In 1930, he made her a gold spiral ring. He thought it would do as a wedding ring, but Louisa called it her engagement ring. So they bought a plain wedding band in Waltham for two dollars.
